chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام
about His, Mighty and Majestic, saying: “And to every one We have appointed heirs from what the parents and the near relatives leave, and those with whom your right hands have ratified agreements”
He عليه السلام said: “Rather, by that He meant the Imams عليهم السلام. By them Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ratified your agreements.”

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّل: Imam al-Rida عليه السلام, the Imam being asked about the verse
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ: the Imams عليهم السلام, identified here as the intended referent
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific for Allah
key_terms.عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ: your oaths or pledges have ratified
key_terms.مَوَالِيَ: heirs or those vested with authority/entitlement in the verse

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida عليه السلام interpret the phrase ‘those with whom your right hands have ratified agreements’ in Qur'an 4:33?
ai.summary: This narration explains the verse as referring, in this context, to the Imams عليهم السلام. It presents the wording about covenants and binding agreements as connected to the authority and designation of the Imams عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of the Mighty and Majestic
[4:33] And to every one We have appointed heirs of what parents and near relatives leave, and as to those with whom your right hands have ratified agreements
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, it Means by that, the Imams<sup>asws</sup>. By them has Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Ratified your agreements’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub who has said that he asked abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) about the meaning of the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High.
“We have chosen heirs for every legacy that parents and relatives may leave. Let those who have been promised a bequest receive their share of the legacy. . .”

[4:33] It is a refrence to the Imams (a.s.) With the Imams (a.s.) Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has established your covenants.” 1. There have been a variety of interpretations of who are the last group of heirs mentioned in this verse, i.e., those with whom you have sworn compact, and, as a result of this, and so as to reconcile these various interpretations with the law, it has at different times been asserted that this verse was abrogated or that it was not. For example, see at.-Taban, at-Taf~ir, vol.5,
